business_overview.one_sentence: BOE Varitronix is principally engaged in automotive and industrial display business, including LCD, TFT products, touch panel display modules and automotive system products.

segments.business_substance: Revenue comes mainly from automotive and industrial display products; management discussion highlights PRC, Europe, America, Japan and Korea customer sourcing regions.
segments.source: Annual Report 2024, Management Discussion and Analysis / Review of Operations

business_overview.revenue_model: Sale of LCD and related display products/modules to automotive manufacturers, Tier-1 customers and industrial customers; revenue is recognised when control of goods is transferred to customers.
business_notes: Revenue growth in 2024 was primarily driven by increased sales of TFT products, touch panel display modules and automotive system products.

Management said 2024 operating profit decreased due to product mix switch, price adjustments, inventory cost, freight charges, overseas exploration expenses, insurance, subcontracting fees and factory consumables.
The company is ultimately controlled by BOE Technology Group Co., Ltd. and has important PRC manufacturing subsidiaries.

profit_cash_conversion.assessment: Reported operating cash flow is strong versus profit, but 2024 was helped by HK$1,431,112k increase in trade and other payables. Maintenance capex is not separately disclosed; 2023 PPE purchase is used as a rough conservative reference and 2022/2024 contain growth expansion effects.

evidence.source: Company IR PDF and local raw filing

evidence.value: Cash resources include cash and cash equivalents, fixed deposits, current other financial assets and restricted bank deposits.
HK$1,154,336k mainland cash and fixed deposits; remittance out of Chinese Mainland subject to foreign exchange control.
Inventories decreased HK$135,717k; receivables/prepayments/contract costs increased HK$719,215k; payables increased HK$1,431,112k.

gaps: No parent-company-only cash and deposit split was disclosed in the extracted report.
No exact split of mainland cash between parent-controlled surplus, operating subsidiary cash and necessary operating cash was disclosed.
Maintenance capital expenditure was not separately disclosed from growth capital expenditure.
Restricted bank deposit conditions were not described in enough detail to test removability, so restricted deposits are treated as non-detachable.
